_doc: Hardware library for the checks (mm). threads: nominal major diameter per thread family as the manifest names it (M2, M2.5, M3: ISO metric; PA2, PA2.5, PA3: self-tapping screws for plastics, major diameter = the number). self_tapping: families that cut or form their own thread in the printed part (mount_check: such a screw fits a plastic hole tapped for the metric thread of its major diameter, PA2 into M2). pilot_pct_of_major: the range the research catalogue cites for self-tapping screws into printed plastic (about 80-90 % of the major diameter, docs/research/design-checks.md S32/S33); a reference band, not a rule. Sleeve sizes are not listed here: the body uses several (4.5 / 3.2, 3.9 / 2.6, 3.6 / 2.2, 3.2 / 2.1 mm outer / inner), so the checks read them from the geometry of the sleeve set pressed into each part (checks.relations sleeve_sets_of).

screw_standards._doc: Dimensions and length series of the head standards, per thread (a thread the standard does not cover has no row; no rows by analogy) (mm). dk = head diameter max, k = head height max (standard values). lengths = nominal screw length l (under the head to the tip) of the standard's preferred series for that thread. lengths_status: the series were transcribed by the builder from the standards' tables and are NOT re-checked against the paywalled texts: treat them as an assumption until compared with the supplier's list (edit them here and every generated screw follows). point_mm: length of the tip cone the engagement counts as not threaded into the hole (assumption, as mount_check.match_screw). density_g_cm3: A2 / 8.8 steel (assumption) for the mass of a generated screw (volume of the modelled envelope x density).
screw_standards.lengths_status: assumption: transcribed from the standards' length tables, not re-checked against the standard text

ISO 7380-1.name: hex socket button head
ISO 7380-1.source: ISO 7380-1:2011 covers M3 and up (https://fasten.it/en/norms/norm/din_en_iso_7380-1, https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/7380/); the M2 / M2.5 rows are vendor catalogue, ISO 7380-1 style, outside the standard's M3+ range, each citing its vendor part series

M2.source: vendor catalogue, ISO 7380-1 style, outside the standard's M3+ range: Aspen Fasteners ME125 series (ME125-204X5, https://www.aspenfasteners.com/m2-0-4-x-5mm-iso-7380-1-metric-button-head-hex-socket-cap-screws-a2-stainless-steel/): head diameter 3.5-3.8, head height 1.16-1.3, hex 1.3. dk = 3.8 (max; the former analogy row had 3.5), k = 1.3 (as before). lengths: the former series, not re-checked against the vendor's stock list

M2.5.source: vendor catalogue, ISO 7380-1 style, outside the standard's M3+ range: Aspen Fasteners ME482 series (ME482-25045X5, https://www.aspenfasteners.com/m2-5-0-45-x-5mm-iso-7380-1-metric-button-head-hex-socket-cap-screws-a4-stainless-steel): head diameter 4.6, head height 1.36-1.5, hex 1.5 (dk / k as the former row). lengths: the former series, not re-checked against the vendor's stock list

M4.source: ISO 4762 M4 dk 7.0 / k 4.0 (https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/4762/; lengths not transcribed)

ISO 7045.name: pan head cross recess screw (type H)

ISO 10642.name: hex socket countersunk head (90 deg)
ISO 10642.source: ISO 10642:2004. dk = theoretical head diameter (sharp edge of the 90 deg cone, max), the diameter of the countersink at the surface the head sits flush in; the actual head edge is smaller (M3: 5.54 min). k = head height max = dk/2 - d/2. The nominal length includes the head (overall length).

ISO 14580.name: hexalobular socket cheese head
ISO 14580.source: ISO 14580:2011 Table 1 (https://cdn.standards.iteh.ai/samples/56456/88025f720d57423b9e2c1ceb78304eec/ISO-14580-2011.pdf), M2 to M10. lengths = the standard's nominal lengths within the range its table gives for the thread; the preferred (bold) series is not marked in the sample text

DIN 7984.name: hex socket low head cap screw
DIN 7984.source: DIN 7984, M3 and up, no M2 / M2.5 (https://fasten.it/en/norms/norm/din_7984, https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/DIN/7984/); length series not found in a public source: no lengths (a builder choosing a length needs the supplier's list)

ISO 1207.name: slotted cheese head
ISO 1207.source: ISO 1207, M1.6 to M10 (https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/1207/): dk max, k max, slot width n nominal; lengths not transcribed

aluminium.note: machine screw into the tapped hole of an aluminium standard part

plastic.note: machine screw: every defined hole of a standard part is a tapped thread (e.g. ROBOTIS XM335 'M2 TAP', the ST3215 case's M2), whatever the case material; thread-forming PA screws go only into printed pilot holes, which are not standard-part holes

nut_standards._doc: Nuts a generated screw ends in (mm). s = width across flats, m = height (max). reference_engagement_mm: the thread length inside the nut that counts as fully engaged = m (the thread end at least at the nut's far face); thread past the far face is reported, not required.

ISO 4032.source: ISO 4032 s, m max, e min (https://www.fasteners.eu/standards/ISO/4032/)

washer_standards._doc: Plain washers (mm): d1 min = hole, d2 max = outer diameter, h = thickness (ISO 7089: min-max as the source gives it, h = its middle; ISO 7092: nominal).

geometry_kinds._doc: Which fastener a hardware part is when neither its body definition (spec.kind) nor a screw_plan says it: from its mesh (fastening/mount_check.py hardware_shape, geometry_kind), only where the declared parts separate. Measured on the selected body's declared hardware (2026-11-23): 271 screws (259 spec.kind screw, 12 screw_plan) all solid on their revolution axis with a wide / narrow end radius ratio 1.75-2.24; 62 washers open on the axis with length / diameter 0.05-0.17; the open parts that are not washers 0.26 and up (41 nuts 0.28-0.38, 22 spacers 0.26-0.71, 10 threaded sleeves 0.77-0.85). Nuts and spacers overlap in shape, so an undeclared nut or spacer stays kind unknown (reported by name: declare it).
